title: Month-end close
goal: Close one company's month under supervision, with a workpaper for every balance-sheet account and reviewer sign-off.
concept_card: A month is closed when every balance-sheet account is supported, intercompany balances match, exceptions are cleared and a reviewer who didn’t prepare the work signs off. Then lock the period in QuickBooks.
lesson_html:
What closing means. The month is closed when every account is correct, supported and reviewed, and QuickBooks is locked so nobody changes it by accident.

Close checklist (per company)

  1. Clear the bank feed and the Uncategorized / Ask My Accountant accounts
  2. Reconcile every bank, credit card and loan account
  3. Record accruals: work done this month but not yet billed
  4. Match intercompany balances with each other company
  5. Review A/P and A/R aging for anything wrong or stale
  6. Check loan balances against lender statements
  7. Reconcile payroll liabilities to the payroll reports
  8. Review the P&L for anything unusual compared with last month
  9. Reviewer signs off, then set the closing date

Balance-sheet reconciliation. For every balance-sheet account, a workpaper shows the QuickBooks balance, the outside proof (bank statement, loan statement, aging report) and the difference, which should be zero or explained.

Intercompany. If Twin Home Buyer shows $12,500 due from Matrix Group One, Matrix must show $12,500 due to Twin Home Buyer. Any difference is an error in one of the two companies.
rule: The person who prepares the close does not approve it.

qbo_steps.title: Trial balance
qbo_steps.html: Reports → Trial Balance for the month end. This lists every account balance.

qbo_steps.title: Find the loose ends
qbo_steps.html: Open ⚙ → Chart of accounts and check the balances of Uncategorized Income, Uncategorized Expense and Ask My Accountant. They should be zero.

qbo_steps.title: Record an accrual
qbo_steps.html: + New → Journal entry. Describe it clearly, attach support, and send it to the reviewer before posting if it's over the approval limit.

qbo_steps.title: Lock the month
qbo_steps.html: ⚙ → Account and settings → Advanced → Accounting → Close the books. Set the closing date and a password held by the reviewer.

qbo_steps.title: Review changes after close
qbo_steps.html: ⚙ → Audit log, or Reports → Exceptions to closing date, to see anything changed in a closed period.

scenario.text_html: At September 30, Twin Home Buyer shows $12,500 due from Matrix Group One. Matrix Group One shows $11,300 due to Twin Home Buyer.
scenario.ask: What is the intercompany difference you must explain?
scenario.explain: $12,500 − $11,300 = $1,200. Look for a payment or transfer recorded in one company but not the other, or coded to the wrong account.
scenario.followup: After close, someone changes a September bill. How would you find out?

quiz.q: Uncategorized Expense has a $3,200 balance at month end. What do you do?
options: Code each item to the right account and project before close
quiz.why: The close isn't done until every item is coded with evidence.
quiz.followup: Twin Home Buyer shows $5,000 due from Equity Track PH. Equity Track PH shows nothing. Where do you look first?

quiz.q: Intercompany balances between two companies should…
options: Be ignored since the same owner owns both
Only be checked at year end
quiz.why: One company's due-from equals the other's due-to. Check every pair monthly.

quiz.q: Why set a closing date with a password in QuickBooks?
options: To stop changes to a finished month without approval
quiz.why: It protects reviewed numbers. Changes after close need the password and show in the audit log.

quiz.q: Who signs off the month-end close?
options: A named reviewer who didn't prepare it
quiz.why: Independent review is the control. You can't approve your own close.

quiz.q: A subcontractor finished work September 26 but sends the invoice October 8. On accrual basis…
options: Record it in September as an accrual
quiz.why: The cost was incurred in September. Accrue it, then reverse the accrual when the bill arrives.

task: Close last month for one company under supervision. Produce the checklist, the trial balance, and a workpaper for each balance-sheet account. Reviewer signs off before you set the closing date.
rubric: Every balance-sheet account has a workpaper with outside proof
Uncategorized and Ask My Accountant are zero
Reviewer sign-off recorded before closing date is set
